text:
lia: Hey team — customer ACME (acct_7d9) says their March invoice has ~3x the token usage expected. They were impacted by the 03:14 UTC incident in us-central where we saw a 504 spike. Billing shows a cluster of short requests counted multiple times. Can we triage? :thinking:
aj: Can you post the invoice id and a sample request id? My hunch is retries + idempotency TTL or header drop. Did client set X-Idempotency-Key?

maria: Invoice is INV-2026-03-1347, customer reached out already. Need per-route/per-request ledger IDs to map charges before we talk credits.

lia: Customer says they used an SDK that sets Idempotency-Key, but they also saw a lot of 504s then immediate client retry. I've attached a snippet they sent (scrubbed):
```
POST /v1/completions 200ms -> 504, client retried with same idempotency-key
POST /v1/completions 120ms -> 200 OK (but counted again in ledger)
```

aj: That pattern suggests the gateway or proxy may have dropped/rewritten the idempotency header for the retry that hit a different backend instance/region. If the Idempotency-Key isn't forwarded to the accounting path, we create a new token tally. Can infra pull proxy logs for X-Idempotency-Key for that customer around 03:10-03:20 UTC?

kyle: Investigating now — we had a small deploy to ingress routing at 03:05 that changed retry fanout behavior for regional failover (intent was to fanout only on cold-starts). Rolling log grep for acct_7d9...

ops-bot: deploy/ingress-routing v1.18.3 deployed by kyle at 2026-03-12T03:05:12Z :rocket:

kyle: Found entries where the header is present on the client req to us-central but missing on the forwarded request to europe-west. Sample log:
```
[03:12:41 UTC] ingress-proxy: client_id=acct_7d9 req_id=rq_abc123 headers={...}
forwarded-request target=eu-west headers={}
```
That explains duplicate counts when retries were routed cross-region.

aj: Ok — two issues then: (1) gateway deploy accidentally strips idempotency header on cross-region forward, (2) our accounting path dedupes only when idempotency key is present and TTL matches. For short-lived TTLs or missing header we double-count.

maria: For remediation: we need per-request ledger ids for all affected requests so billing can be reconciled. If duplicate ledger entries map to same client-visible request, we'll propose a credit. Lia — can you run a list of request IDs and forward to billing?

lia: Working on it. I can pull the ledger rows using the time window and acct_7d9. Will post CSV. Suggest holding customer credit until we confirm the mapping.

kyle: Patch incoming — I'll revert the forwarding behavior for cross-region retry and add a unit test to ensure idempotency headers are preserved. Also extending our ingress->accounting header passthrough whitelist so X-Idempotency-Key cannot be dropped. ETA 2 hours. :shipit:

aj: Also recommend increasing idempotency-key TTL on the ledger side from 2m to 10m for transient network flaps; less risk of legitimate duplicate charges. I'll open a config PR.

maria: Fine with provisional credit if we can show a tight mapping. Keep me posted on the CSV.

lia: Uploaded preliminary CSV (snip): request_ids that appear to have duplicate ledger rows: rq_abc123, rq_def456, rq_ghi789. Sending to billing thread.

aj: Quick grep command I used to find header drops if helpful: 
```bash
jq -r 'select(.client_id=="acct_7d9" and (.timestamp|startswith("2026-03-12T03:"))) | {req_id:.req_id, forwarded_headers:.forwarded_headers}' /var/log/ingress/*.log | grep -B1 X-Idempotency-Key
```

kyle: Will follow up with a hotfix deploy and post the rollout plan. If anyone sees more affected customers, escalate here.

maria: Thx. Once ledger mapping is done we'll draft the customer-facing credit and explanation. Prefer "root cause: cross-region retry header loss during transient outage" rather than deep infra details.

lia: Copy. I'll coordinate message and refund once we have final list. :eyes:
